BREAKOUT_MOMENTUM: Enters long when price closes above its recent breakout high, above its 200-period moving average, and RSI confirms momentum (one variant additionally requires above-average volume). Exits on an ATR-based stop, a fixed target, or a timeframe-aware maximum holding period, whichever comes first.
TREND_PULLBACK: Enters long only within an already-established uptrend (50-period average above the 200-period average, price above both), after price has recently pulled back to the 50-period average and closed back above it, with RSI confirming a neutral pullback rather than a reversal. Exits on an ATR-based stop, a fixed target, or a timeframe-aware maximum holding period.
VOLATILITY_SQUEEZE: Watches for a run of unusually narrow Bollinger Bands -- the lowest percentile of their own recent history, sustained for several consecutive candles -- a classic 'coiling' signal that volatility is about to expand. Enters long on a breakout above the high reached during that squeeze, filtered by a trend moving average. Exits on an ATR-based stop, a fixed target, or a timeframe-aware maximum holding period.
COINTEGRATION_PAIRS: A statistical-arbitrage signal on the BTC/ETH price ratio: when the ratio's z-score moves far enough from its rolling mean, it enters the underperforming leg expecting the ratio to revert. Because Vatican is long-only paper trading, this only simulates one leg of what would be a true market-neutral pairs trade -- its P&L reflects that single leg's own price move, not a genuine hedged spread return.
NEWS_SENTIMENT: A forward-test-only signal that scores recent, sufficiently-aged news headlines (at least 2 hours old, to avoid lookahead bias) for bullish or bearish sentiment and reports a directional bias. It has no historical backtest -- no trustworthy backdated headline-timestamp dataset exists -- so it is evaluated purely on live, forward-going evidence.
ORDERFLOW_IMBALANCE: Reads live order-book depth (top 20 levels) and compares total bid volume to total ask volume; a sufficiently lopsided ratio, combined with price on the same side of its 20-period moving average, triggers a directional entry. Exits when the imbalance reverts or an ATR-based stop is hit. Order-book snapshots have no historical replay, so this strategy has no backtest at all -- every result comes from live forward-testing only.
RANGE_MEAN_REVERSION: Only trades while the market is genuinely ranging (ADX below 25, a trend-strength filter checked before every entry) -- inside that regime, it buys when price drops meaningfully below its 20-period average (below the lower Bollinger Band) expecting a bounce back toward the mean, and shorts the mirror-image setup above the upper band.
GOLD_SILVER_RATIO_MR: Trades mean-reversion in the gold/silver price ratio, which oscillates within a historical band. When the ratio is unusually high -- judged by a rolling 252-session percentile, not a fixed historical band, so it isn't permanently skewed by one-off events like the 2020 COVID spike -- it goes long silver and short gold, expecting the ratio to fall back, and the mirror trade when the ratio is unusually low.
PEAD: Trades the well-documented 'post-earnings-announcement drift' effect: prices tend to keep drifting in the direction of an earnings surprise for days afterward. Enters the day after a company's earnings announcement in the direction of the surprise, sized by how large that surprise was. Tested only on 7 large, currently-successful companies -- a real survivor-bias caveat that applies to every result this strategy reports.
DONCHIAN_TREND: A bidirectional Donchian-channel breakout strategy: goes long on a breakout above the N-period high, short on a breakdown below the N-period low. Exits use a fixed 2x-ATR stop, a fixed 2:1 reward-to-risk target, and an explicit maximum holding period -- a materially different, bracket-style exit from this family's original long-only, trailing-exit version.
